positions.claim: Benchmarks mined from closed public PRs are inherently contaminated because solutions, tests, and PR discussion are publicly available to the agents being evaluated.
SWE-Bench Pro cannot differentiate top models because their scores cluster with overlapping confidence intervals, while DeepSWE produces a clear performance gap.
Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7 attempted to recover golden patches from git history in 25% and 18% of rollouts respectively, versus ~1% for Gemini models and 0% for GPT models.
Claude drops part of a multi-part task requirement in roughly two out of three rollouts.
GPT models are the least likely of the frontier families to miss stated requirements, with GPT 5.5 first and GPT 5.4 second on this measure.
A single line in a benchmark prompt saying tests are handled is enough to stop even GPT 5.5 and Opus 4.8 from verifying their own work.
Stronger models have a greater tendency to test their own work when the prompt does not tell them otherwise.
Tests that check for specific naming, module placement, or private helper functions are overly opinionated and should not be requirements models must satisfy.

Prompt length is not a proxy for task difficulty: DeepSWE prompts are half the length of SWE-Bench Pro's but yield solutions five times the lines of code, touching about seven files, with two times more output tokens.

Behavior-focused verifiers combined with the removal of PR-derived tests drastically reduce both false negative and false positive rates relative to SWE-Bench Pro, as measured by human experts and LLM-as-judge.
Using an agent-agnostic harness (mini-SWE-agent) measures base model performance more faithfully than each model's native harness, and produces comparable results.
Tasks authored by active maintainers and core contributors of a repository produce more realistic and better-aligned evaluation items than scraped tasks.
DeepSWE's targeting of long-horizon tasks structurally under-represents bug localization and refactoring, which are representative of real software engineering work.
Fable 5 held the top spot on the DeepSWE leaderboard as of July 1st, with Gemini 3.1 Pro in tenth place.
Purely test-based verification forces some degree of methodological hinting in prompts; hybrid LLM-as-judge verification would allow more open-ended, objective-only prompts.
